items.stem: What is the term used to describe the period when the bright portion of the Moon increases?
Which of the following best explains why the Moon is sometimes visible during the day?
Based on the passage, which of the following best describes the cycle of the Moon's phases?
If a student observes the Moon at sunrise on a day when it is in the waxing phase, where would the Moon be located in the sky?
If a person observes the Moon at sunset on a day when it is in the waning phase, what would they expect to see?
Why does the illuminated portion of the Moon seen from Earth decrease when it appears closer to the Sun?
Based on the diagram in Fig. 11.5a, which position of the Moon corresponds to the waning gibbous phase?
A student observes the Moon at the same time on two consecutive days and notices that the bright portion is decreasing. What can the student infer about the Moon's phase?
If the Moon is in position H as shown in Fig. 11.5a, what phase would be observed from the Earth?
In the diagram in Fig. 11.5a, which position of the Moon corresponds to the Full Moon phase?
If the Moon's orbit were not tilted with respect to Earth's orbit around the Sun, which of the following would be true?
Which of the following best explains why the Moon appears different on different days?
If the Moon is overhead today, when will it be overhead again?
What is the purpose of marking the tip of a stick's shadow every minute?
If a person finds the shortest shadow at 12:20 p.m. today, what time will the Sun be at the same position tomorrow?
How long does it take for the Sun to return to the same position in the sky?
If a festival is based on a purely lunar calendar, what can be said about its date in the Gregorian calendar?
Which type of calendar combines elements of both solar and lunar calendars?
What is the main reason for the difference between the lunar and solar year?
Which of the following is a reason for the shift in dates of festivals based on the sidereal calendar?
Which figure in the chapter shows the Moon's crescent always facing towards the Sun?
Based on the information in the passage, which of the following statements is true about the Moon's phases?
If a person observes the Moon rising in the East just as the Sun is setting, which phase of the Moon is most likely?
If the Moon is seen as a full Moon, how long would it take for the same phase to appear again in the same location?
A student observes the Moon and notices that the illuminated part of the Moon changes shape every day. What causes this change in shape?
The passage states that the dates of festivals based on the sidereal calendar slowly shift away from the solstices and equinoxes. What is the main reason for this shift?

The passage explains that the Moon's phases are caused by the changing portion of its illuminated side that we see from Earth. Which of the following best describes why the Moon's phases repeat in a cycle?
What is the name of the calendar that combines elements of both solar and lunar calendars?
The passage mentions that the Moon takes about 50 minutes longer to complete one orbit around the Earth than it takes to complete one rotation on its axis. What does this mean?
If a festival is based on the phases of the Moon, on which day of the month does it usually fall?
Which of the following is NOT a use of artificial satellites?
According to the passage, why do some festivals fall on different dates in the Gregorian calendar each year?
A student observes the Sun's position at sunrise and notices that it rises slightly north of East in summer and slightly south of East in winter. What does this observation indicate?
Why are luni-solar calendars used in India to celebrate festivals?
Based on the passage, which of the following is true about the length of a solar day?
Why does the illuminated portion of the Moon seen from the Earth decrease when it appears closer to the Sun?
Which natural event is the basis for defining a day?
Which natural event is the basis for the unit of a day?
Why are intercalary months added to some calendars?
Which of the following correctly describes the direction in which the crescent Moon faces?
What is the basis for the statement that the Moon's crescent always faces the Sun?
A student wants to observe an artificial satellite in the night sky. When is the best time to look for it?
If the Moon is seen as a crescent in the evening, in which direction would it be located?
Why does the Gregorian calendar include a leap year every four years?
